PR seems somewhat incomplete - when I delete `assets/overlays/gcp-pd/generated` directory and try to re-generate the assets it fails:

```
make update-generated-assets
hack/update-generated-assets.sh
assets/assets.go:7:28: pattern overlays/*: cannot embed directory overlays/gcp-pd: contains no embeddable files
make: *** [update-generated-assets] Error 1
```

This is because `collectConfigs()` is not wired to load `CSIDriverGeneratorConfig` (which is missing) - this is what @rhrmo pointed out. 

Also, there's a typo in the binary in PR description: `./bin/gcp-pd-csi-driver-smb-operator` -> smb

I was thinking that this PR could be an intermediate step where you just intend to demonstrate a working binary - however the switch from legacy directory in Containerfile would indicate that the migration to generated files is finished. 

When I worked on AWS migration I implemented this in a single [PR](https://github.com/openshift/csi-operator/pull/237), not saying it's the only right way but I think that first we need to get the generators working and see CI tests are passing with those assets. Then cross-check the assets with the legacy ones - it's easy to misss something.

@RomanBednar , @rhrmo , thank you for review, I fixed a typo in PR description -- nice catch!

You are right, the PR is intermediate. It provides the operator binary that works in manual tests and passes CI, but based on pre-defined assets. The next step is to auto-generate assets with generator machinery. SMB operator went through the same process: compare https://github.com/openshift/csi-operator/pull/205 vs. https://github.com/openshift/csi-operator/pull/217.

> however the switch from legacy directory in Containerfile would indicate that the migration to generated files is finished

I'd prefer to make this switch as early as possible to see CI failures (and any other complains) earlier and have time to fix them before the end of the cycle. Let me know if you prefer other approach -- keep the PR open until everything is done and polished before the merge.

@mpatlasov I don't mind if we don't have the code to generate assets right now, I was just unsure why it was not there yet, we can merge this PR without the generation code. I left a unit test suggestion, but we do not need to switch to the library right now as getting this PR merged is a priority. I don't think the e2e tests are failing because of changes from this pr and required ones seem to be passing. 
/lgtm

> Let me know if you prefer other approach

I don't have a strong opinion in that, I just fail to see what's the benefit of the phased approach :) why would we want manually created assets in "generated" directory at any point? It's the same approach as having the assets from GCP PD operator repo copied here to legacy dir and testing with those right? That way you know CI setup and builds are ok, and then I would start generating the assets and comparing them to legacy (static) ones. Or are the legacy files anyhow different from the current ones in "generated" dir? If so, how and why? 

I think we can merge this as long as the generator skips GCP PD (which it does now) so it does not get in way of other PRs and `verify-generated-assets` check. I'm just trying to understand the reasoning.

> I'd prefer to make this switch as early as possible

Yes, it's easy to miss something. So you want to merge this first and then start working on the generator stuff? I think the approach is fine, but it's a significant portion of this effort. I remember it was quite tricky to convince the generator to do the right thing when I migrated EFS a while ago.
other than the comment typo it looks good to me

🧹 Nitpick comments (2)
pkg/driver/gcp-pd/gcp_pd.go (1)
`36-39`: _📐 Maintainability & Code Quality_ | _🔵 Trivial_ | _⚡ Quick win_ **Fix malformed log call and redundant/non-idiomatic error message.** `klog.Error(nil, "...")` treats `nil` as a `fmt.Print`-style argument (klog's `Error` args are "handled in the manner of `fmt.Print`"), so this prints something like `Flavour HyperShift is not supported!` instead of a clean message. Additionally, this error is already logged again by the caller (`RunOperator` logs `"error building operator config: %v"` on any non-nil error from this builder), so the local `klog.Error` call is redundant. The `fmt.Errorf` message is also capitalized and ends with `!`, which violates Go's error-string convention (lower-case, no trailing punctuation).
🔧 Proposed fix ```diff if flavour != generator.FlavourStandalone { - klog.Error(nil, "Flavour HyperShift is not supported!") - return nil, fmt.Errorf("Flavour HyperShift is not supported!") + return nil, fmt.Errorf("flavour %q is not supported", flavour) } ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. In `@pkg/driver/gcp-pd/gcp_pd.go` around lines 36 - 39, The gcp_pd builder’s unsupported-flavour branch is logging incorrectly and returning a non-idiomatic error. In the config builder path in `gcp_pd.go`, remove the local `klog.Error(nil, ...)` call because `RunOperator` already logs builder failures, and change the returned `fmt.Errorf` message to a lowercase, punctuation-free error string. Keep the check on `flavour != generator.FlavourStandalone` and ensure the branch only returns the clean error. ```
